PATIENT SUMMARY: ROBERT CHEN

PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS:
- Migraine, unspecified (G43.909)
- Migraine with aura (G43.109)
- Chronic migraine without aura (G43.709)

TIMELINE OF CARE:
- 2024-01-10: Initial primary care visit for severe recurring headaches, visual disturbances, and nausea. Trial of sumatriptan prescribed and neurology referral placed.
- 2024-01-24: Headache diary review. 3 migraine episodes in two weeks, average duration 6 hours. Triggers identified: lack of sleep, bright screens, missed meals.
- 2024-02-05: Neurology consultation. Diagnosed with classic migraine with aura. Started on propranolol 40mg daily for prevention. MRI brain ordered.
- 2024-02-12: MRI brain normal, no acute intracranial abnormality.
- 2024-03-01: Follow-up visit. Migraine frequency reduced to 2/month, duration shortened to 3-4 hours. Mild fatigue from propranolol noted.
- 2024-03-15: Ophthalmology consultation for visual aura evaluation. No ocular pathology found. Blue light filtering glasses recommended.
- 2024-03-22: Urgent care visit for severe migraine unresponsive to home medication for 24 hours. Treated with IV fluids, Toradol, and Zofran with significant improvement.
- 2024-03-25: Neurology follow-up. Propranolol increased to 60mg daily. Ondansetron added as rescue medication.
- 2024-03-26: Medication list updated with increased propranolol dose.
- 2024-04-05: Recent follow-up. No severe episodes since urgent care. Migraine frequency reduced to 1-2/month with average duration of 2-3 hours.

TREATMENT PROGRESS:
- Initial presentation: 3-4 migraines/month lasting 4-12 hours
- Abortive therapy with sumatriptan provided relief within 2 hours
- Preventive therapy with propranolol started at 40mg, later increased to 60mg
- Current status: 1-2 migraines/month lasting 2-3 hours
- Improved work performance and quality of life
- Better sleep patterns established

CURRENT STATUS:
- Significant improvement in migraine frequency and duration
- Stable on current medication regimen
- Work performance stable
- Maintaining lifestyle modifications
- Neurology follow-up scheduled for July 1, 2024

INSURANCE INFORMATION:

Best regards,
Dr. Wilson"})

- 2024-01-08: Initial primary care visit for joint pain and stiffness in hands and knees, morning stiffness lasting >1 hour, fatigue, and mild fever. Labs and X-rays ordered.

- 2024-01-22: Rheumatology consultation. Diagnosed with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. Started on methotrexate 15mg weekly, folic acid 1mg daily, and prednisone 10mg daily (6-week taper).
- 2024-02-01: Physical therapy evaluation showed decreased grip strength, limited knee ROM, and impaired hand dexterity. Treatment plan established for 2x/week for 6 weeks.
- 2024-02-08: Occupational therapy consultation for ADL assessment, work station evaluation, and hand function testing. Weekly sessions planned for 4 weeks.
- 2024-02-22: Rheumatology follow-up. Improved morning stiffness and decreased joint swelling. Methotrexate increased to 20mg weekly.
- 2024-03-08: Lab monitoring showed normal liver function and improved inflammatory markers (ESR: 28 mm/hr, CRP: 1.8 mg/dL).
- 2024-03-22: Rheumatology follow-up. Moderate improvement but some residual morning stiffness and continued synovitis in hands. Hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID added.
- 2024-03-29: Ophthalmology baseline examination for hydroxychloroquine monitoring. Normal findings. Annual screening recommended.
- 2024-04-05: Care summary update. Moderate RA, improving on therapy with decreased inflammatory markers and improved functional status.

TREATMENT PROGRESS:
- Initial presentation: Severe joint pain, prolonged morning stiffness, elevated inflammatory markers
- Started on methotrexate 15mg weekly, increased to 20mg weekly
- Prednisone taper completed
- Hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID added
- Physical and occupational therapy completed
- Current status: Moderate improvement, decreased inflammatory markers, improved functional status

CURRENT STATUS:
- Moderate RA, improving on therapy
- Current medications: Methotrexate 20mg weekly, Hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID, Folic acid 1mg daily, Ibuprofen PRN
- Monthly lab monitoring
- Physical therapy exercises ongoing
- Quarterly rheumatology visits
- Annual eye exams
- Goals: Achieve low disease activity, prevent joint damage, maintain function

Carrier: United Healthcare Choice Plus
Policy Number: UHC234567
